title: Embryonic development: germ layers, neurulation and organ formation
description: Follow gastrulation, ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm, neural tube, somites, cardiac loop and limb buds through early organ formation.

questions.question: What are the three embryonic germ layers?
questions.answer: Gastrulation establishes ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. Together they contribute to later organs and tissues, though any one organ often draws from more than one layer.

questions.question: What does the embryonic neural tube form?
questions.answer: It contributes to the brain and spinal cord. It forms after neural plate folding and closure; the microscopic folding process is not directly visible on the generic external development image.

questions.question: When does major embryonic organ formation occur?
questions.answer: A standard developmental convention describes much organ-plan formation during roughly weeks three through eight after fertilization. Obstetric gestational weeks counted from the LMP are usually about two weeks higher.

questions.question: How does a flat embryonic disc become a body shape?
questions.answer: Head, tail and lateral folds transform the disc into a three-dimensional body and help position the primitive gut. The still digital plate shows a simplified later form, not actual folding in motion.

questions.question: Is the illustrated early human an exact image of week eight?
questions.answer: No. It is a stylized non-diagnostic model rather than a measured clinical image or week-specific specimen. Form and timing vary, so age cannot be determined from the rendering.
